title: Hand (figure_6) fails in SnappingCarve.placeNodes: T-mesh nodes 40 and 41 both landed on copy vertex 2699
description:
Found while fixing PATCH-109 (the motorcycle null edge hit). With that fix ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_6/hand_in_tri.off clears buildMotorcycleGraph with a clean arrangement (152 traces, 3640 arcs, 1861 nodes, 1745 patches, 0 Def 3.1 violations) and then fails in the T-mesh embedding:

```
IllegalStateException: T-mesh nodes 40 and 41 both landed on copy vertex 2699; one mesh vertex never owns two T-mesh nodes
  at SnappingCarve.placeNodes (SnappingCarve.java ~191)
```

placeNodes gives every T-mesh node a copy vertex: a node with vertexId >= 0 claims the copy of that source vertex (claimSourceVertex), a node inside a face mints one by splitting (mintInside). The check fires when the second node resolves to a copy vertex already owned by the first. Nodes 40 and 41 are spawn-origin nodes (created from the singularity ports before the event simulation runs), and the PATCH-109 agent saw the identical error with the same node ids and copy vertex under a completely different arrangement during diagnosis, so the collision is fixed by the input, not by the trace geometry. Most likely two ports of one singularity vertex each produced a node with the same source vertexId (a valence-3 or valence-5 vertex spawns several traces, and the port nodes should share one T-mesh node, not be one node per port), or two distinct singularities were snapped onto the same mesh vertex upstream in the cross field or the seamless map.

Decide which and fix at that layer: either merge co-located spawn nodes into one T-mesh node when the arrangement is built, or make the singularity extraction refuse two singularities on one vertex.
definition-of-done: 1. hand (figure_6) runs through buildTMesh in QuadLayoutScene once PATCH-109 lands. 2. The ticket records what nodes 40 and 41 are (their ports, singularity vertex and index) and why both carry source vertex 2699. 3. The fix is at the layer that created the duplicate, with a test on a hand-authored arrangement of two ports on one vertex. 4. rockerarm, botijo, elk and fandisk report the same node and arc counts in the [motorcycle] and T-mesh log lines as before.
testing-plan: 1. In a worktree synced after PATCH-109 lands, load hand in QuadLayoutScene and reproduce. 2. Print nodes 40 and 41 (kind, port ids, source vertex, singularity index) at the failure. 3. Trace back to the spawn code in MotorcycleGraph and the singularity list from the cross field. 4. Fix, rerun hand; if it fails at a later stage record that as a new unknown. 5. Screenshot under tmp/ and compare the four other meshes' log lines.
changes-made: Answer to unknown 1: neither. Nodes 40 and 41 are two trace-crossing nodes minted at one point of the surface - mesh vertex 2699 - one attributed to active face 3380 and one to 4875, the two faces of that vertex's fan. Their chart positions are bit-identical: node 40 vertexId=-1 activeFace=3380 uv=(-43.99226664155535, 10.475873259011564), node 41 vertexId=-1 activeFace=4875 with the same uv. Neither is a spawn-origin node: hand seeds 40 singularity nodes (ids 0-39) and spawnFromSingularities already shares one node per singularity vertex through nodeByVertexId, so two ports of one cone can never mint two nodes.

Why it surfaced as 'lies in no child face of source face 4875' rather than the collision the title names: node 41's chart position is vertex 2699's own uv, but inverting face 4875's chart rounds it to barycentric [-1.55e-15, 1.09e-15, 1.0000000000000004] - a rounding step OUTSIDE its own face. SnappingCarve.mintInside gates the child search on an exact ExactBarycentricOrient sign, so the only child face holding it is rejected and the search falls off the end. Under the arrangement PATCH-109 produced, the same two nodes rounded to the inside instead and hit the 'both landed on copy vertex 2699' throw. Same defect, two faces of the same coin.

Root cause behind the coincident nodes: traces 114 and 127 are the SAME separatrix, traced from both ends. It joins cone 2568 (node 31) and cone 3101 (node 34), and each cone spawns a port along it, so both traversals run the identical curve and node every point of it twice. The patch-diag port dumps show it directly - node 40 carried four ports in only two directions ((arc 2607 out dir=1,0 key=0.0000) with (arc 2937 in key=0.0000), (arc 2606 in key=3.1416) with (arc 2938 out key=3.1416)) - two collinear strands laid on top of each other.

Fix 1 (MotorcycleGraph.nodeAtChartPoint) - one T-mesh node per point of the surface. Every crossing mint site (handleIntersection, registerSegment's retroactive sweep, handleTermination and finalizeOpenTraces) now resolves its node through one method instead of calling new EmbeddedNode. A point on a mesh vertex is pinned to that vertex (vertexId set, activeFace -1) and shared across the whole fan through the existing nodeByVertexId map, so the carve reaches it by claimSourceVertex and never inverts a chart for it. A point on a mesh edge is shared by the edge's two faces, keyed by the parameter along the edge measured from its lower-numbered endpoint, which both charts agree on. A point inside a face is shared with any node already standing there. The tolerance throughout is FaceChordWalk.MINIMUM_SEPARATION (1e-9), the carve's own snap rule, so the arrangement can no longer carry two nodes the carve would be forced to place on one copy vertex.

Fix 2 (new ChartBarycentric in the embedding package) - the chart inversion, the corner/edge/coincidence predicates and a clampOntoTriangle, all at MINIMUM_SEPARATION, in one place. SnappingCarve.chartBarycentric now delegates to it and clamps, so a node whose barycentric the inversion rounded a step below zero is pulled onto its face instead of matching no child face. A coordinate further out than the tolerance is left alone, so a genuine face/position disagreement still throws.

Fix 3 (MotorcycleGraph.handleEdgeCrossing) - a face exit that lands exactly on a corner is now routed through ChartWalker.crossVertex, which is what the walker's own contract says ('an exactly-zero corner offset is reported via cornerLocalIndex; the caller must then route through crossVertex'); handleEdgeCrossing called crossEdge instead, so a separatrix ran straight through a cone rather than stopping at it. crossStalledBoundary already did this correctly - the edge path was the one site that did not. On hand this is 4 corner exits, 2 of them on cones. It takes the arrangement's lawViolations from 146 to 0, removes both stalledBoundaryCrossings, and makes the quantization separation loop converge (3 rounds, no cuts left) where before it ran the 50-round cap and ended with '[quantize] VALIDITY VIOLATION merged singularity vertices=[230, 2568]'.

Fix 4 (MotorcycleGraph.dropTracesCoveredByAnother) - subdivideArcsAtMeetings now builds the chains, drops any trace whose chain another already runs forwards or backwards, forgets the meetings that dropped trace induced on the survivors, and rebuilds the chains once more before emitting arcs. Without the second rebuild the survivor still broke at the dropped trace's crossing nodes, leaving degree-2 nodes mid-separatrix and two 5-corner cells ('patch 641 is not a valid rectangle'). On hand exactly 1 trace is dropped (traces=152 covered=1); on bolt, rockerarm and buddha none is.

hand (figure_6) now loads end to end in QuadLayoutScene - no 'failed to load', and the log reaches '[quad-layout] patch surfaces 0.076s'. Stage line: cross field 0.538s, seamless 0.684s (meanDistortion 0.16835723261213387, the exact value recorded before this change, flippedTriangleCount=0), motorcycle graph 0.148s, quantization 0.384s, carve 0.522s, contract 1.809s, global grid map 3.024s, patch surfaces 0.076s. Arrangement: '[motorcycle] done traces=152 (covered=1) arcs=3537 nodes=1809 patches=1731 retroactiveCrossings=56', Def 3.1 rectangularity violations=0, hop-turn lawViolations=0, no invalid cycles. Carve: '[embed] arcs=3537 copy V=13805 E=41409 F=27606'. New diagnostics on hand: '[motorcycle-diag] cornerExits=4 ofThoseOnCones=2' and '[motorcycle-diag] crossingsOnVertex=3 sharedVertexNodes=2 sharedEdgeNodes=2 sharedFaceNodes=0'. Screenshot tmp/patch-114-hand.png (full quad layout over the hand), log tmp/patch-114-hand-quadlayout.log; the pre-fix failure is kept at tmp/patch-114-repro.log.

The other three meshes are unchanged and all load end to end. bolt: meanDistortion 0.18121096246751692 and '[embed] arcs=1398 copy V=7665 E=22989 F=15326' - both identical to the values PATCH-107 recorded - '[motorcycle] done traces=80 (covered=0) arcs=1398 nodes=721 patches=679', patch surfaces 0.024s. rockerarm: meanDistortion 0.2441987734694241 (identical), '[embed] arcs=2706 copy V=43603 E=130809 F=87206', traces=120 (covered=0) arcs=2706 nodes=1383 patches=1323, patch surfaces 0.171s. buddha: meanDistortion 0.2317070343554014 (identical), '[embed] arcs=17916 copy V=157881 E=473637 F=315758', traces=528 (covered=0) arcs=17916 nodes=9092 patches=8826, patch surfaces 0.101s. None of the three prints a [motorcycle-diag] line for corner exits or shared crossing nodes and none has a covered trace, so every new code path is inert on them and their arrangements are bit-identical. Screenshots tmp/patch-114-bolt.png, tmp/patch-114-rockerarm.png, tmp/patch-114-buddha.png.

Tests: two new hand-authored unit classes, no mesh loaded and no pipeline run. unit.mesh.CoincidentCrossingNodeTest (9 cases) is the collapse in miniature - two triangles sharing the vertex the crossing lands on, at hand's own chart magnitudes: it asserts cornerHolding names corner 2 for hand's literal failing barycentric [-1.5543122344752192E-15, 1.0917910056726295E-15, 1.0000000000000004] even though the first coordinate is negative, that both faces of the fan resolve one chart point to the same mesh vertex, that both faces of an edge measure a point on it at the same parameter, that the clamp pulls a rounding step back onto the face while leaving a genuinely outside point outside, and that two points a few ulps apart are one point while distinct ones are not. unit.mesh.CollinearTrailOverlapTest (2 cases) pins the precondition for the duplicate-trace drop: two chords of one face on the same iso-line run opposite ways are reported as a contact, and a chord on the next iso-line over is not. Full unit suite: Tests run: 304, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0.

Diff: ixdar-app/src/main/java/.../motorcycle/MotorcycleGraph.java, .../motorcycle/records/Trace.java (one flag), .../embedding/SnappingCarve.java, .../embedding/LayoutEmbedding.java, new .../embedding/ChartBarycentric.java, plus the two test classes. SnappingCarve and LayoutEmbedding also gained failure diagnostics that made this ticket tractable and are worth keeping: describeNode and describeSourceFaceCorners name the nodes and the face's corner owners on both placeNodes throws, assertSubcomplex now prints the first double-claimed copy element with both arcs, and 'arc N was never carved' names its trace and endpoints.
